parts.gloss: those who are capable of action

words.gloss: towards those who are capable of powerful action

literal: If ruin is desired, act without listening; if destruction is desired, commit offense towards those who are capable of action.
translation: If one desires ruin, let them act without listening to advice; if they desire swift destruction, let them commit an offense against those who have the power to act.
modern: ஒருவர் தன் அழிவை விரும்பினால், நல்லோர் அறிவுரையைக் கேட்காமல் செயல்படட்டும்; தன் முடிவை விரும்பினால், ஆற்றல் மிக்கவர்களிடம் தவறு செய்யட்டும்.
explanation: This couplet uses powerful irony to warn against self-destructive behavior. The poet suggests that if a person is determined to ruin themselves, they can simply act blindly without listening to any wise counsel. However, if they want to guarantee their immediate and complete destruction, they should go a step further and offend those who possess great power and capability. The word 'āṟṟupavar' highlights individuals who have the strength and means to execute actions, while 'iḻukku' refers to the fatal mistake of transgressing against them.
